titulo: UPS Layoffs: $457,000 to Shareholders per Job Cut
caption:
UPS Layoffs: $457,000 to Shareholders per Job Cut

UPS layoffs, 14,000 positions: $457,000 in buybacks and dividends for every job cut, using UPS's own 2025 numbers.
From the archive: Jan 2026. Not today's news.
UPS, Jan 27, 2026 (UPS, Q4 2025 earnings release): "right-size our business to create a more efficient operating model"

Why did UPS lay off workers? In its fourth-quarter 2025 earnings release (the report a public company files with the SEC, the U.S. market regulator), dated January 27, 2026, UPS describes a workforce reduction of approximately 14,000 positions, completed in 2025, in those words. This short strikes the phrase through and puts next to it a number from the same company and the same year.

The math: $6.39 billion to shareholders, 2025, company-wide ÷ about 14,000 positions = $457,000 in buybacks and dividends per job cut.
What counts as "to shareholders": a buyback is a company buying its own stock; a dividend is cash paid out to people who own that stock. UPS's 2025 10-K (its annual report to the SEC) lists $1,000 million of stock repurchased plus $5,398 million of dividends in 2025, company-wide (cash flow statement, in millions). The 14,000 positions is UPS's own approximate figure, from its earnings release. Both figures are for 2025.

Efficient, for whom? (Our take.)

Do you know someone who has been through a round of cuts? Send this to them.

Synthetic voice. Sources: UPS Q4 2025 release (SEC), Jan 27, 2026; UPS 2025 10-K (SEC), Feb 17, 2026.

More at the link in bio.
